steps: Permit & location

Get a permit and check local codes; a W.E.T.T. or N.F.I. qualified installer is recommended. The floor needs adequate load-bearing capacity (load-distributing plate if not); keep out of traffic areas; securing the unit in position is recommended. Never connect to air distribution ductwork.
Floor protection

Non-combustible ember protector under the full width and depth of the unit, including the vent pipe, extending 6" (152mm) at the front. The side extension is given as 6" beyond the door and ash pan openings in the text, and as 2" in Figure 12 (from the edge of the top) and on the rating label.
Outside air

Optional except in mobile homes or where codes require: 2" (51mm) ID non-combustible pipe, max. recommended 10ft. (3m), 3" (75mm) beyond that. Exterior intake well below the flue termination with a screen; never from a garage or unventilated crawl space.
Clearances & alcove
Front 48", side 6" from edge of top, back 3" from back of hopper; corner per Figure 13. Alcove: min. height 7 ft., min. width 36 in., max. depth 36 in. Vent at the vent manufacturer's clearances.
Plan the termination

Check the lettered clearances (A–M). At least 12 inches (30 cm) from the wall and 24" (60 cm) above the roof, two feet from combustibles, exhaust above the inlet elevation, never in an enclosed or semi-enclosed area.

Lettered vent-terminal clearances (Figure 14). Local codes may require different clearances.

A · above grade12 inches (30 cm) above non-combustible grade; 24 inches (60 cm) above grass, plants, wood, or a combustible veranda, porch, deck or balcony
B · window or door that opens48 inches (120 cm) beside or below; 18 inches (45 cm) with fresh air installed; 12 inches (30 cm) above
C · permanently closed window12 inches (30 cm), recommended against condensation
D · ventilated soffit within 2 feet (60 cm)36 inches (76 cm); 18 inches (45 cm) with fresh air installed
E · unventilated soffit12 inches (30 cm)
F · outside corner12 inches (30 cm)
G · inside corner12 inches (30 cm)
H · gas meter / regulatornot above it within 3 feet (90 cm) horizontally of the regulator center-line
I · service regulator vent outlet6 feet (1.8 m)
J · non-mechanical air supply inlet4 feet (1.2 m); 12 inches (30 cm) with fresh air installed
K · mechanical air supply inlet10 feet (3.1 m)
L · above public paved sidewalk / driveway7 feet (2.1 m); never directly above one shared by two dwellings
M · under veranda, porch, deck, balcony12 inches (30 cm), only if fully open on at least 2 sides beneath
Note: the table on p. 22 prints clearance D (ventilated soffit) as 36 inches (76 cm); its inch and metric figures don't agree.

Termination requirements (p. 23)

  • Never in enclosed or semi-enclosed areas: carport, garage, attic, crawl space, narrow walkway, closely fenced area, under an enclosed sun deck or porch, stairwells, covered breezeway.
  • Exhaust above the inlet elevation; a minimum of 5 feet of vertical pipe is recommended to prevent smoke or odor at shutdown or in a power failure.
  • Terminate at least 12 inches (30 cm) from the wall; a vertical termination protrudes at least 24" (60 cm) from the roof surface.
  • At least two feet from shrubs, plants, grass, fences, roof overhangs and adjacent buildings.
  • Exposed vent in high-traffic areas may need non-combustible shielding or guards.
Install the pellet vent

3" or 4" Type PL / L pipe (UL 641 / ULC S609) on the 3" collar: silicone and three screws at the starter pipe, screw non-locking joints, thimble or firestop through combustibles, clean-out tee at the horizontal-to-vertical transition. 4" for horizontal runs over 10 feet or more than 3 elbows.
Chimney options

Masonry chimney: an approved 3" or 4" stainless steel liner kit all the way up, with top plate and rain cap. Existing 6" ID wood stove pipe: approved adapter (p. 24). No flue damper; never share a flue with another appliance.
Mobile home extras

Outside air required; lag-screw to the floor through the pedestal holes or the leg anchor tabs; ground to the steel chassis in addition to the cord ground. Never in a sleeping room; keep the floor, wall and roof structure intact.
Initial set-up: damper

During the first burn, trims at 3: after 15-20 min. on high set the damper for 0.10-0.12 in. w.c.; then on Heat Level 1, after 5-10 minutes, read 0.09" to 0.11" and correct with the combustion blower trim.

1. Fit a low pressure digital vacuum gauge or magnehelic with a sealed 1/8" metal probe in the port above or to the side of the ash pan door.
  2. Remove the left side panel; the damper is against the back of the air jacket. Loosen its locking screw.
  3. Start the stove and check both factory trims (combustion blower and auger) are at 3, the middle position.
  4. After 15-20 min. on high, set the damper for 0.10-0.12 in. w.c. Pull it out toward the outside of the stove to increase firebox vacuum; push it in to reduce.
  5. Turn down to Heat Level 1 (LOW), wait 5-10 minutes and read again: 0.09" to 0.11". If not, adjust the combustion blower trim: hold the hidden button under the "TH" in TRUE NORTH and use the heat level arrows. The light that is out shows the setting.
  6. Tighten the damper locking screw and refit the left side shield.

Re-set the draft when changing grade of fuel (p. 25). The combustion blower trim is a last resort, used only after the damper is set.
Thermostat (optional)

Unplug; open the right cabinet side and remove the 2 screws holding the main board to the hopper; land both low-voltage thermostat wires on the double screw terminal block. Mount it away from radiant heat, drafts, dead spots and duct air.

items: No power → check the cord is plugged in and the household circuit breaker
High limit switch faulty or tripped → dealer / service

panels.title: Pellets won't drop into the liner
items: Hopper lid open → close it; lid switch damaged → dealer / service
Sawdust / pellets plugging the auger → clear the auger system
Vacuum switch / lines plugged or damaged, or combustion blower blocked or damaged → check switch and vacuum hose for damage or kinks; check / clean venting
Auger motor fuse blown → check the motor for visible signs of a short; if OK, replace the fuse (wiring diagram)

items: Burn pot / liner not installed correctly → reinstall properly
Igniter hole in liner restricted or plugged → clean liner holes and igniter tube
Igniter fuse blown → check fuse; if blown, check igniter for visible damage

panels.title: Turns off while operating (code 3)
items: Fire went out or too cold → see 'Won't turn on' and 'Pellets won't drop'
Low grade fuel → trim auger feed up for more heat
Check firebox vacuum levels; adjust if needed (Initial Set-up)
Ash build-up in venting → clean venting as required

codes: Stove did not light, fire went out, or stove went cold while in operation
Hi limit switch is open — stove overheated

light.title: Starting and stopping the stove
light.html:
Before each start, check that the holes in the burn pot liner (the cup the pellets burn in) are clear, and that the liner is pushed back against the igniter tube.

  1. Prime it if it's empty. The first time, or after the hopper has run out, the auger that feeds pellets is empty. Put a handful of pellets in the middle of the liner, or hold the Auger button until pellets begin to drop.
  2. Press ON/OFF. The power light turns red and a 15-minute lighting sequence starts: the auger loads the burn pot, the igniter lights the pellets, then feeding resumes. A little smoke in the firebox is normal.
  3. Wait for green. Once it's lit, the power light turns green and the stove burns at the level shown on the heat level lights.
Don't restart mid-sequence — the burn pot will overload with pellets. If it isn't lit after 15 minutes, the middle heat level light flashes. Once it has cooled, empty the unburned pellets from the liner and start again. Never tip them into the hopper: pellets that seem cool can still ignite others.

Turning it off

Press ON/OFF. The power light turns orange and the panel lights go out. The auger stops, but the fans keep running until the exhaust has cooled and the shutdown cycle is done — up to 20 minutes, depending on how hot it was running.

pellets.title: Pellets and the hopper
pellets.html:
Burn only premium wood pellets. In the U.S., buy pellets graded by an EPA-approved organization: Pellet Fuels Institute, ENplus or CANplus. Your dealer can recommend a type.

These void the warranty: any fuel not approved for this stove, and "dirty" pellets with dirt, chemical binders or high salt. Never burn cord wood, garbage, rubber, plastics or flammable fluids.

Filling the hopper

Lift the top of the stove to reach the hopper. It holds up to 80 pounds (36 kg). Check for foreign objects before you pour, and keep the lid closed: the auger won't run while the lid, door or ash drawer is open. Store pellets at least 48" (1.2 m) from the stove.

What the pellets should meet

Densityover 38 lbs/cuft
Sizeunder 1.5 in., diameter .230 to .285
Chloridesunder 300ppm by weight
Trace metalsunder 100mg/kg
Note: the fuel list on p. 7 gives the ash limit as under 1% for inorganic fines (ash content), and two lines later as under 2% for ash content.

Hardwood pellets generally make more ash than softwood ones, and high-ash fuel can mean cleaning every day.

heat.title: Heat levels and thermostat modes
heat.html:
Use the heat level arrow buttons to choose a setting. The five heat level lights show it: #1 (far left) is low, #5 (far right) is high.

Thermostat modes

A slide switch on the panel picks the mode. The stove leaves the factory in manual mode; the other two need an optional low-voltage wall thermostat (not provided).

ManualBurns at your heat level until you change it or turn it off.
HI/LOBurns at your heat level while the thermostat calls for heat, then drops to the lowest level, until turned off or out of fuel.
AutoLike HI/LO, but after 45 minutes at the lowest level with no call for heat it shuts off, and relights when the thermostat calls.

On a thermostat you still press ON/OFF for the first burn, and again if the stove runs out of pellets and shuts off with a fault code.

Pellets burning too low or too hot?

Never hand-feed pellets; that over-fires the stove. If it goes out during long periods on low, hold the Auger button (four lights on, one off) and press the up arrow to feed more. If low is still too warm, press the down arrow. This changes the feed across the whole range, so go easy. The factory setting is 3.

clean.title: Burn pot cleaning and schedule
clean.html:
The burn pot liner has holes in its bottom and sides that feed air to the pellets. Impurities can bake into clinkers (hard lumps of minerals or sand) that block them, so check the liner every day.

Shut the stove down, unplug it and let it go cold first.

  1. Open the door and lift the liner out.
  2. Vacuum the ash out of the burn pot.
  3. Scrape out any clinkers and clear every hole, with a small pointed object if needed.
  4. Put the liner back with the igniter hole toward the back, pushed against the igniter tube so it seals.

How often

Burn pot linerdaily, depending on fuel quality
Burn potevery 5 bags (schedule) · about 5 - 10 bags (cleaning section)
Ash pan, leg modelevery 15 bags
Ash pan, pedestalevery 30 bags
Flue gas passagesonce a year or every one to two tons (50-100 bags)
Use an ash or shop vacuum with a fine dust filter, never a household vacuum, and never vacuum hot ash.

A yearly service by a trained professional is strongly recommended.

ash.title: Ash pan and glass
ash.html:
Only take the ash pan out when the stove is off and cold.

  1. Turn the latch counter-clockwise to release the pan.
  2. Lift the pan up, then pull it out.
  3. Empty the ashes into a metal container with a tight-fitting lid, and set it on a non-combustible surface well away from anything that burns. If you bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until every cinder is cold.
  4. Vacuum out the ash pan enclosure if it needs it.
  5. Push the pan in until the bottom catches and drops down. Check it sits tight to the face of the enclosure, then tighten the latch.
Latch it tight. A pan that doesn't seal makes extra smoke and creosote. Left open far enough, it trips the vacuum switch, stops the auger and shuts the stove down. Never put unburned pellets in the ash pan; they can start a fire there.

Cleaning the glass

With the stove cold, turn the door handle clockwise to horizontal and pull the door open slowly, so ash isn't drawn out. Wipe the glass with a soft cloth or paper towel and a non-abrasive household glass cleaner or wood stove window cleaner. Don't use abrasive cleaners.

sounds.title: That sound or smell is probably normal
sounds.html:
Normal sounds

  • Rushing air and small creaks when the blowers come on. The lower the burn rate, the slower the fan.
  • Pellets dropping into the burn pot.
  • The auger motor pulsing on and off.
  • Now and then, a crack as the auger cuts a pellet in half.

The room fan comes on by itself once the stove warms up, changes speed with the burn rate, and keeps running after the auger stops until the stove has cooled. The first time the stove is plugged in, the combustion blower runs for 10 minutes.

The first-fire smell

The high-temperature paint finishes curing the first few times you burn on high, and some parts carry a light coat of machining oil. Both can give off unpleasant odors at first. Open the windows to air out the room.

Some smoke inside the firebox while it lights is expected too.

Not normal: if the fire changes dramatically during extreme weather, stop using the stove right away.

trouble.title: Flashing lights and quick checks
trouble.html:
If the stove shuts down unexpectedly, look at the heat level lights:

#3 light flashingIt didn't light, the fire went out, or it went cold while running.
#4 light flashingThe high-limit switch is open: the stove overheated.

Quick checks

  • No lights or fan noise after 30 seconds: check the power cord is plugged in and check your circuit breaker. If those are fine, the high-limit switch may be tripped or faulty; call your dealer.
  • Pellets won't drop: check the hopper isn't empty and the lid is closed. Sawdust or pellets may be plugging the auger.
  • Pellets won't light after 8-10 minutes: make sure the burn pot and liner are seated properly and the liner holes and igniter tube are clear.
  • Goes out while running: with low-grade fuel, trim the auger feed up (see "Set the heat"). The venting may need cleaning.
  • Fans won't stop after shutdown: it can take up to 20 minutes to cool. If they keep going, call your dealer.

Other causes, like a damaged lid switch, the vacuum switch or hose, or a blown fuse, need a qualified service technician. Before restarting, let the stove cool and empty unburned pellets from the liner.

outage.title: When the power goes out
outage.html:
• Power returns while the stove is still hot: it goes into its start-up sequence and keeps running.
  • Power is off long enough for the stove to cool: when it returns, the exhaust blower runs for 10 minutes to purge any smoke.
  • On a thermostat in Auto mode: it won't start lighting until the thermostat calls for heat again.
Note: p. 10 says that when the power comes back, a stove on a thermostat in Auto mode won't start its ignition sequence until the thermostat calls for heat; p. 11 says that with a thermostat connected you have to press ON/OFF when the power to the stove is interrupted.
Carbon monoxide (CO): when the blowers stop in an outage, some CO can get into the room until the last pellets in the burn pot go out. A CO detector in the same room is recommended.

Generators and surges

The stove may run on a portable generator, but some generators' regulators don't suit its electronics. The better the generator (the smoother its output), the better the odds. A surge-protected power bar is recommended to protect the electronics from surges and lightning.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• The outside of the stove gets hot enough to burn. Keep children, clothing and furniture away, watch young children closely in the room, and don't let children or pets touch it when it's hot.
  • Keep furniture, wood, paper, drapes and anything else that burns at least 48" from the front, 6" from each side and 3" from the back.
  • Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or freshen up a fire, and keep them away from the stove.
  • Don't open the door or clean the glass while it's running or hot. Never run it with the glass cracked, broken or removed, and refit any grill, panel or glass taken off for service.
  • Plug it straight into a grounded three-prong outlet and never remove the grounding prong.
  • Smoke detectors are recommended, and a CO detector in the same room; your local code may require one.

If the chimney or vent catches fire

  1. Call the fire department.
  2. Put out the fire in the burn pot liner with a cup of water and close the door.
  3. Check the flue pipes, chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire. Use a fire extinguisher or garden hose if needed.
  4. Don't use the stove again until you're sure the chimney and its lining aren't damaged.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
True North warrants the stove to the original consumer purchaser. It isn't transferable.

Firebox, castings, glass3 years parts (1 year labour)
Electrical components and switches1 year parts and labour
Gaskets, paint (peeling), bricks, firebox liner, burn pot and liner1 year parts only

Glass is covered for thermal breakage only, not impact.

Not covered

  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, lack of maintenance, over-firing, negligence, shipping accidents, power failures, downdrafts or venting problems.
  • Scratches, corrosion, warping or discoloration from over-firing, abrasives or chemical cleaners.
  • Burning materials the stove isn't EPA-certified for, not following the owner's manual, or unauthorized parts: any of these voids it.

An authorized qualified technician must install it. A one-time replacement limit applies to covered parts.

Making a claim

Contact your True North dealer with proof of purchase (dated bill of sale), the purchase date, model name and serial number. Register the stove at truenorthstoves.com/register; the serial number is on the product certification label or the cover of your installation manual.

specOutput.title: Heat output & emissions
specOutput.html:
EPA tested output7,400 to 28,200 BTU/hr
Maker's website: BTU High 40,000; BTU Low 28,200.
EPA certified emissions1.36 g/hr
Certified CO emissions0.05 g/min
LHV / HHV efficiency78.9% / 72.2%
Max feed rate (p. 7)approx. 4.5 lbs/hour

Meets the 2020 EPA PM limits using premium wood pellets. Efficiencies are weighted averages tested to CSA B415; the output range is based on that efficiency and the EPA-test burn rates. Rating label: tested to method 28R and ASTM E2779-10. The manufacturer-set minimum low burn must not be altered.

Note: the EPA specifications on p. 4 give the input rate as approx. 10,000 Btu to 39,500 (depending on fuel type); the rating label on p. 33 gives it as 9,000 - 40,000 Btu/Hr.

specSize.title: Weight & hopper
specSize.html:
Weight325 pounds (147 Kg.)
Hopper capacityup to 80 pounds (36 Kg.)

Hopper results vary with fuel density. Overall dimensions are given only on the drawing on this page (Figure 11), so they aren't transcribed here.

The floor needs adequate load-bearing capacity; if it doesn't have it, take suitable measures such as a load-distributing plate (p. 19).

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Supply120 volts, 60 Hz
Maximum5 Amps
Normal operating2.5 Amps
Plugthree-prong (grounding)

Plug directly into a properly grounded three-prong, 120 volt, 60 Hz receptacle; never cut or remove the grounding prong. Don't route the cord under or in front of the unit, and keep it off hot or sharp surfaces (p. 5). A surge-protected power bar is recommended. Mobile homes: also ground the stove to the steel chassis (p. 25). Fuses are shown on the wiring diagram (p. 29).

Note: the specifications on p. 4 give the current rating as 5 Amps maximum and 2.5 Amps normal operating; the rating label on p. 33 gives 120V A/C, 4.3AMP, 60Hz.

specVent.title: Pellet venting
specVent.html:
Pipe3" (76mm) or 4" (102mm) Type PL or Type L pellet vent
ListingUL 641 and ULC S609
Starter flue collar3" outside diameter
4" recommendedhorizontal runs over 10 feet (3 m), or more than 3 elbows
Altitude over 4000 feet4" (102mm) suggested
  • Silicone the vent to the starter pipe and fasten with three screws; on pipe without a locking system, screw every joint with three screws. Seal joints externally with high temperature silicone or aluminium tape if required.
  • Approved wall thimble or ceiling firestop through combustible walls or ceilings (CAN/CSA-B365 and local codes); keep the vapor barrier effective.
  • Include a tee with clean-out at the horizontal-to-vertical transition.
  • Horizontal-only terminations are approved, but a minimum 5 ft. (1.5m) of vertical is recommended to help keep smoke in during power failures. Vertical through the eaves is ideal against wind.
  • Stainless steel single wall pipe only as a liner inside a masonry or approved wood burning chimney.
No flue damper in the exhaust venting. Don't connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance or to any air distribution duct.

specAir.title: Outside combustion air
specAir.html:
Intake2" (51mm) ID non-combustible pipe
Max recommended length10ft. (3m)
Longer runincrease the intake supply tube to 3" (75mm)
Requiredmobile homes, and where local codes require

Locate the exterior intake substantially below the flue termination, with a screen cover against weather and pests. A well ventilated crawl space is acceptable; never draw from an enclosed space (garage, unventilated crawl space).

The stove isn't designed for a negatively pressurized room. Outside air through flexible or rigid pipe greatly reduces that risk but may not eliminate it (p. 6). With fresh air installed, vent-terminal clearances B, D and J are reduced (p. 22).

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Front48" (1.2m)
Side6" (152mm) from edge of top
Back3" (76mm) from back of hopper
Corner (rating label)3 in. / 76 mm
Alcovemin. height 7 ft. (2.13 m), min. width 36 in. (92 cm), max. depth 36in. (92 cm)
Flue center16-1/2" (419mm) above the surface the stove rests on

Install the vent at the clearances its manufacturer specifies. Minimum clearances may not leave room for operation and maintenance, and the unit may have to be removed for servicing, especially in a 36 in. wide alcove. The recommended clear zone in front is 4 feet (1.2m). Corner and wall layouts are drawn in Figure 13.

specFloor.title: Floor (ember) protection
specFloor.html:
Install on a non-combustible ember protector that runs the full width and depth under the heater, including under the vent pipe.

Front6" (152mm)
Material (rating label)continuous non-combustible, UL 1618 type 1
Back (rating label)under vent tee if installed
Note: the text on p. 20 says the protector extends an additional 6" (152mm) beyond each side of the Firebox Viewing Door and Ash Pan openings; Figure 12 on the same page shows the side extension as 2" (50mm) from edge of top, and the rating label (p. 33) gives sides 2 in/51 mm.

specDraft.title: Damper & draft set-up
specDraft.html:
Set the damper after installation, during the first burn, and again when changing grade of fuel (p. 25). Use a low pressure digital vacuum gauge or magnehelic on a sealed 1/8" metal probe in the port above or to the side of the ash pan door.

High, after 15-20 min.0.10-0.12 in. w.c. (set with the damper)
Heat Level 1, after 5-10 minutes0.09" to 0.11" (set with combustion blower trim)
Auger & combustion blower trimsfactory 3 (middle)

The damper is against the back of the air jacket, behind the left side panel; loosen its locking screw first and tighten it after. Pull it out toward the outside of the stove to increase firebox vacuum, push it in to reduce. Too much draft reduces efficiency; too little causes sooting and creosote.

review.notes: One manual (Installation & Operation, 36 pp.); physical pages match the printed page numbers. No French-only safety text and no scrambled-font text found. Ignition: ON/OFF button starts a 15-minute automatic lighting sequence with an electric igniter (parts list: 'Ignitor, 400w'); no other ignition modes. Not transcribed because they exist only in figures: overall dimensions (Figure 11, p. 18, unlabelled values), the wall/corner clearance drawing (Figure 13, p. 21; the 3 in. corner clearance is taken from the rating label text, p. 33), the vent-terminal drawing (Figure 14, p. 22; the A-M values come from the text table), and the fuse ratings on the wiring diagram (p. 29; 2 A, 2 A, 3 A, 5 A cannot be matched to circuits from the text). The routine-maintenance table on p. 12 marks each item weekly / monthly / yearly with an X whose column is lost in the text, so only its 'or every N bags' / daily notes are used. Burn pot interval differs mildly: table 'every 5 bags' vs text 'about 5 - 10 bags' (both p. 12); both are shown. Troubleshooting chart (p. 17): the layout doesn't make clear whether 'Check/Clean venting system' pairs with the vacuum-switch row or the combustion-blower row, so those two causes and their solutions are grouped in one item. p. 27 prints the high-fire draft reading as '0.10-0.12n.w.c.'; rendered as 0.10-0.12 in. w.c. Rear firebox liner part number: 80001351 in the parts list (items 29 and 36) and the Figure 5 caption (p. 14) vs SKU 80002272 in the Figure 6 caption (p. 15); no part numbers are used in the guide. Some printed cross-references point to the wrong page (p. 8 cites p. 10 for thermostat operation, which is on p. 11; p. 17 cites p. 26 for the wiring diagram, which is on p. 29, and p. 3 for the auger trim, which is on p. 10). Listing standards are taken from the cover (p. 4 prints 'ULC 627S'; the label prints 'ASTM E 1509-12' and 'ULC S627-00').
